Browse 10581 plugins Install a plugin GitHub npm 中文

The plugin market
inside DeepSeek Harness

Browse and search 10581 community plugins, install with one click — most go live without even a restart. Updates, uninstall, live install progress. No telemetry, ever.

dsh plugin --profile web add dshmarket
Then restart dsh web → Plugins → Plugin Market tab (dsh 0.2.1+; Settings → Plugin Market on older hosts). That's the whole setup.

This catalog is also a plugin market index. On dsh 0.2.1+, open Plugins → Discover → Index sources and add https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dsh-plugin-catalog/index.json — the list as a format-1 index, served from npm so it loads quickly everywhere (the GitHub Pages copies at awesome-dsh-plugin.com/index.json and dshmarket.com/index.json are the same document). The Discover tab and the plugin_market agent tool then search the same plugins.

Guides

How the market and DSH behave, and what to do when something looks wrong. Each guide answers one question.

  • Why an update says "waiting": the release-age wait

    A new plugin version is held for a set time before DSH will install it. What the wait is, why it exists, how dsh web and the desktop app differ, and how to change it.

  • "Installed, not in effect": what each plugin state means

    Every status the Installed tab can show — in effect, restart needed, incompatible, library, failed — what it means and what to do about it.

  • What the permission labels on a plugin mean

    Plugin pages list what the code appears to do: read files, use the network, run commands. Each label in plain terms, and what a static scan can and cannot tell you.

  • Desktop app or dsh web: where your plugins live

    The desktop app and dsh web each keep their own plugin list. How to install in each, and why a plugin you installed may seem to be missing.

  • "The plugin market stopped running": what happened and what to do

    Why the market page can report that it stopped after an install or update, what to try in order, and what happened to the operation you were running.

  • The DSH plugin ecosystem in numbers

    How many DSH plugins exist, how fast the catalog grows, which categories dominate, how concentrated installs are, and what plugins ask to do. Computed from the catalog on every rebuild.

  • We installed the most downloaded DSH plugins

    A clean DSH, the market's own install button, the most downloaded plugins. Which ones worked straight away, which needed a restart or your approval, and which need a newer DSH.

What dsh-market is

🛒

Everything, in one place

The full curated catalog from awesome-dsh-plugin — categories, star counts, top/new sorting, bilingual descriptions.

⚡

Fast installs

npm tarballs are preferred over full-repo GitHub downloads whenever a plugin publishes to npm — typically seconds.

✨

No restart, mostly

Most plugins are live right after a page refresh. Updates and uninstalls take one click too — the market even updates itself.

🧩

Zero jargon

Missing a component? The market detects it and fixes it with one button. You never see a terminal.

🔒

Guard rails

Installs are restricted to the curated registry, build scripts stay blocked by default, and terminal-surface plugins are flagged before you install them.

Private by default

Common questions

What is a plugin?

An extension that adds something to dsh: a different interface, another model, a new tool, access from your phone. Uninstall it any time.

How do I install one?

Install this market first (the command above), then press Install in the market. To install from a terminal, or when an install fails, see the install guide.

Does it cost anything?

The market and the list are free and open source (MIT). Plugins are published by their authors; check each plugin's own page for whether it charges.

Do I need to restart dsh?

Most plugins are live after a page reload; a few need one restart of dsh web. If the plugin shows up under Settings → Plugins, it installed.
